QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_35

question.text: Amortizing bonds are those in which:

answer.text: The principal is repaid gradually over the life of the bond through periodic payments that include both interest and principal
The entire principal is repaid only at maturity in a single lump sum
No principal is ever repaid and the bond continues indefinitely
The coupon rate increases every year until maturity

explanation.text: The Logic: In an amortizing bond the principal is repaid over the life of the bond rather than only at maturity, and each periodic payment includes both interest and principal. Auto loans, consumer loans, and home loans are examples of amortizing structures. The Trap: Option B describes a bullet (plain vanilla) bond. Option C describes a perpetual bond. Option D describes a step-up coupon structure. Note: The defining feature is the blended interest-plus-principal cash flow over the bond's life — not how that split varies year to year.
